Find, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram $ABCD.$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946476/assets/dafaf2421aaa9be80c472b4dde7c941defb94f7f3533fda4ebb2fdcee2b60e31.png)

In square units rounded to the **nearest tenth**, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $△ABD$ and $△BDC$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946476/assets/cd9363a3cc686ae45f49c982f4b31ad75b7c7897dcf7e8af58e530dba6946e1d.png)

First we find the area for $△ABD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 7\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{50}^{∘} \\  & =21\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{50}^{∘} \\  & ≈16.086\,9,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Now we find the area for $△BCD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{BDC} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 7\cdot 8\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{43}^{∘} \\  & =28\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{43}^{∘} \\  & ≈19.096\,0,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & ={A}_{ABD}+{A}_{BDC} \\  & ≈16.086\,9+19.096\,0 \\  & ≈35.182\,9\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, to the **nearest tenth**, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $35.2.$
